newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes higher on exports, cold weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes higher on exports, cold weather.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on bullish input from the export sector and on jitters about cold weather in portions of the U.S. winter wheat growing region, traders said.

Algeria this week announced a tender to buy 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat and there was news overnight that Egypt and Iran were expected back in the world grain market soon to buy wheat for May and June shipment. Most exporters said they saw the possibility of sales of roughly 200,000 to Iran and 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes to Egypt.
But cold weather was central to the wheat futures gains.

Weather and crop sources early Wednesday said snow and cold blanketed much of the central U.S. early Wednesday and a second blast of cold forecast for Thursday and Friday could damage winter wheat in Kansas and Nebraska.
"All of this is related to a late-season Arctic high pressure system currently centered over the Red River Valley," said Joel Burgio, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp.
Cargill Inc bought one million bushels of July and Merrill Lynch Futures bought 800,000 bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat closed unchanged to 3-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with May up 3-1/2 at $3.85-1/2.
